latest.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
latest.summary: An observer sees only part of the surrounding world, yet must keep track of what lies beyond the current view. Spatial perception therefore involves more than recognizing individual images: it calls for a persistent spatial state that is updated under self-motion and used to guide action. Do visual foundation models provide representations that support such a state? We study this question through four levels of spatial capability---spatial structure, object persistence, predictive spatial update, and actionability---using frozen-feature probes on ten representations under streaming egocentric observations of static indoor environments. latest.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
latest.summary: Video generation is shifting from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic generation, where planning, tool use, and feedback enable coherent, controllable multi-shot videos. In parallel, video world models provide action-conditioned observations and predicted futures, serving as interactive environments for agents. We study their intersection through the agent harness: an executable runtime that constructs context, exposes tools, maintains state, routes feedback, and manages budgets around video models. This report examines three directions. First, agentic video generation, where harnesses coordinate scripting, shot planning, asset management, production, and editing, alongside the evaluation…

latest.title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
latest.summary: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.

latest.title: A Biophysical Framework for Force-Induced Mitochondrial Branches.
latest.summary: Mitochondrial networks are shaped not only by fission and fusion but also by mechanical forces. Here, we examine pulling-induced branch formation and contrast it with fusion-based branch formation. Live imaging reveals that branches formed by pulling are shorter-lived but initiate more frequently and with a narrower range of angles, concomitantly inducing deformation in parent mitochondria - in contrast with those formed by fusion. In addition, perturbations to microtubule stability and motor protein association with mitochondria alter pulled branch lifetimes, emphasizing the role of cytoskeletal dynamics in branch stability. We developed a mechanical model based on free energy…

latest.title: The Pauli Spin Algebra, Related Clifford Algebra Representation, and Derivation of the Dirac Hamiltonian Operator
latest.summary: I present a novel approach to derivation of the Dirac Hamiltonian operator on the secondly quantized Fock space, based on the the Pauli spin \(\text{su}{(2)}\) - algebra and its Clifford algebra representation. The relativistic Lorentz invariance of the related Schrödinger equation is stated as a natural consequence of its operator structure.

Here, we characterised LSSF with Trametes versicolor across culture volumes and inoculation strategies. The biomass accumulation model described a trade-off between colonisation speed and biomass accumulation. items.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
items.summary: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. We show that this algorithmic separation is not fundamental. By deriving suitable RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, we place all of these stages under a single likelihood-based training algorithm, unified training. This perspective turns the foundation-model training lifecycle into a problem of choosing which data to train on, in what proportions, and when, with conventional staged training as a special case. We instantiate this framework in a unified…

items.title: TRACER, a time-to-event EHR foundation model for disease detection across health systems
items.summary: Foundation models trained on longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can predict clinical diagnoses years in the future, making them a potential tool for disease screening. We developed TRACER (Temporal Risk Assessment with Clinical EHR Representations), a decoder-based foundation model pretrained on data from over 4.5 million patients from four health systems, and evaluated it on 16 incident diseases at 1-, 2-, and 5-year horizons in more than 2 million patients from two health systems excluded from model development. In contrast to typical evaluations that focus on global metrics (e.g., AUROC), we measured performance at the low false-positive rates that are realistic for…

items.title: Dynamic Powergrid Optimization with FPGA-based Neuromorphic Higher-order Ising Machines
items.summary: The advent of large, high-density FPGAs such as the AMD Versal enables efficient hardware implementation of neuromorphic Ising machines, unlocking unprecedented performance for complex combinatorial optimizations. A critical application for this computing paradigm is dynamic powergrid optimization, specifically Distribution Network Reconfiguration (DNR), which seeks to mitigate severe resistive losses and reduce electricity costs by optimizing network switch configurations in real time. This paper presents an FPGA-based neuromorphic higher-order Ising machine for high-speed, adaptive DNR. By directly mapping DNR onto higher-order Ising interactions via a polynomial unconstrained binary…

items.title: ML-COHP: predicting bond descriptors using latent space of a universal interatomic potentials
items.summary: The integrated crystal orbital Hamilton population (ICOHP) is the standard measure of bond strength in a DFT calculation, but every structure needs its own DFT single point and LOBSTER projection, which takes days for a cell of a hundred atoms, such as a grain boundary or a catalytic nanoparticle. We predict ICOHP from the frozen descriptors of a MACE foundation model. A symmetric pair head reads the scalar and bond-projected vector channels of the two atoms and corrects a pair baseline built from the element embeddings of the same model. We tested the model on the high-entropy diboride (Hf,Zr,Ti,Nb,Ta)B$_2$, Pt clusters on defective graphene and Pt/Pd nanoparticles with adsorbed O$_2$.…

items.title: A Pretrained Model for Bayesian Filtering in Heterogeneous Dynamical Systems
items.summary: Filtering has not yet had its foundation-model moment: state estimation is still dominated either by online Bayesian filtering algorithms that require known dy- namics as inputs, or by learning-based neural filters trained from scratch for a single system or parametric family. The core challenge is structural heterogene- ity: dynamical systems differ in their governing dynamics, physical scales, and noise levels, precluding a shared representation space for a reusable filter. To bridge this gap, we introduce FilterFM, the first pretrained model for Bayesian filtering that estimates latent states across heterogeneous dynamical systems with a single checkpoint. FilterFM employs a…

items.title: Quasinormal-mode encounters: Pseudospectra near Kerr--Newman exceptional points
items.summary: Exceptional points (EPs), at which two quasinormal frequencies and their eigenvectors coalesce, can strongly enhance the spectral instability of black hole quasinormal modes. We investigate this behavior in Kerr--Newman spacetimes through pseudospectra and condition numbers for neutral massless scalar fields and coupled gravitoelectromagnetic (GE) perturbations. For the scalar field, we follow the $(\ell,m)=(1,1)$ spheroidal branch and derive the energy norm from the stress-energy tensor. For GE perturbations, we use a coupled four-field system equipped with a positive radiative energy. At the selected near-EP backgrounds, the condition numbers of both modes in the close pair exceed those…

items.title: Scalar--photon coupling in cosmology: Radiation evolution, recombination, and CMB signatures
items.summary: Interactions between a cosmological scalar field and radiation can modify the pre-recombination expansion history and leave observable signatures in cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies. We investigate an effective scalar-photon-fluid coupling, deriving the coupled background and linear perturbation equations and leading-order adiabatic initial conditions for a canonical scalar field with an exponential potential. Starting from a radiation-era scaling solution, we implement the dynamical interaction in CLASS and compute the resulting recombination history, CMB anisotropies, and linear matter power spectrum. Photon thermodynamics and collisions are treated phenomenologically,…

items.title: Towards fNIRS foundation models: A curated corpus of 67 public datasets with channel positions in MNI space
items.summary: Brain foundation models have transformed medical artificial intelligence and computational neuroscience by reducing the reliance on task-specific data through large-scale pretraining. While they have been successful with non-invasive neuroimaging data, their adoption in functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has lagged due to the limited size and heterogeneity of public datasets, which are collected under varying protocols, devices, and sensor configurations. In addition, no single fNIRS dataset is comparable in size to the largest datasets in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), or magnetoencephalography (MEG). items.title: Celia: Catalog Embeddings Learned from cosmologIcal simulAtions
items.summary: Cosmological hydrodynamical simulations connect observed galaxies to cosmology and the physics of galaxy formation. Each simulation is expensive, and different codes model galaxy formation in different ways. We present Celia (Catalog Embeddings Learned from cosmologIcal simulAtions), a self-supervised foundation model that maps catalogs of subhalos and their galaxy properties to an embedding vector for the purposes of compression and organization of astrophysical and large-scale structure information. Celia is pretrained without parameter labels on the IllustrisTNG, SIMBA and Astrid suites of CAMELS and their N-body counterparts, by reconstructing masked subhalo properties and predicting…

items.title: Understanding axial attention in TSFMs through single location regression
items.summary: Recent advances in Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) increasingly rely on axial attention mechanisms, but despite their empirical success, the theoretical properties of axial attention remain largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we extend the Single Location Regression framework introduced in Marion et al. [2025] to 2D structured data, in order to study sparse information settings where a target depends on a small number of tokens. We formulate an analytically tractable axial attention-type predictor and rigorously analyze its statistical properties and training dynamics. items.title: Gravitational waves away from a Schwarzschild black hole: full spectrum analysis
items.summary: Gravitational waves as one approaches Schwarzschild null infinity are the core of our investigation, treated as the spin-weighted generalisation of a massless scalar field. In particular, we compute their full spectrum, consistent with observations coming from LIGO and VIRGO experiments. This paper continues recent work by the authors, where the Poincaré asymptotic expansion was exploited in black hole perturbation theory. The mathematical formalism we developed is now intimately connected with gravitational wave phenomenology, providing new mathematical tools to investigate their features.

items.title: Learning Safe Flow Matching Robot Policies from Binary Feasibility Oracles
items.summary: Robot foundation models increasingly rely on flow-based action generation for general-purpose manipulation, yet the generated actions are not guaranteed to satisfy physical constraints such as joint limits and collision avoidance. This problem is especially challenging when the feasible set cannot be described analytically and is accessible only through black-box feasibility oracles. We study this practical oracle-only setting and propose an oracle-guided differentiable safeguard for safe flow-matching robot policies. items.summary: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. items.title: Phenomenological implications of cosmic (super)strings with time-varying tension
items.summary: Cosmic strings and cosmic superstrings could have formed in the early universe. In a particular class of models, the tension associated with these defects is time dependent, either because the strings themselves are composed of evolving moduli fields, or because they are directly coupled to evolving scalar fields leading to an effective time dependence in the string tension. Here we take seriously the possibility of this time dependence and investigate the phenomenological consequences of such an evolution, comparing the results to the more traditional case of a fixed time independent tension. In particular, for five different time varying models, motivated by different possible forms of…

items.title: Spectral Invariant Fusion and Refinement for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
items.summary: Domain generalized semantic segmentation is challenging because it requires accurate dense prediction on unseen domains without any access to target-domain data during training. Existing methods improve transferability through data diversification, invariant learning, or direct use of foundation models, but they often struggle to simultaneously suppress domain-sensitive interference and preserve fine-grained spatial cues. In this work, we propose SIFR, a frequency-aware dual-stream framework that tackles domain shift at both the fusion and decoding stages. SIFR uses spectral modeling as a unified principle to regulate both heterogeneous prior interaction and dense decoder refinement.…

items.title: Split Quaternion Toolbox: A MATLAB Implementation
items.summary: This paper presents a MATLAB toolbox for working with split quaternions and split quaternion matrices. Split quaternions, also known as coquaternions, form a four-dimensional associative non-commutative algebra over the real numbers with a signature (+,+,-,-). The toolbox provides two main classes: SplitQuaternion for scalar-valued split quaternions and SplitQuaternionMatrix for matrix-valued split quaternions. The implementation includes arithmetic operations, algebraic functions, matrix operations, linear algebra utilities, and various conversion methods. The toolbox is designed to be intuitive for users familiar with MATLAB's standard matrix operations while providing the full power of…

items.title: Efficient Low-Rank Approximation of Quaternion Matrices via Adaptive Cross Approximation
items.summary: The adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm is a powerful tool for constructing low-rank matrix approximations using only a small subset of matrix entries. While extensively studied for real and complex matrices, its extension to quaternion algebras, remains largely unexplored. This paper presents the first comprehensive framework for adaptive cross approximation operating natively in the quaternion algebra H. Unlike approaches that rely on real embeddings or complexifications, our method preserves the algebraic structure of quaternions throughout the computation, avoiding information loss and maintaining the natural correlations between quaternion components. items.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vignéras
items.summary: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. items.title: AI at a Turning Point: From ChatGPT through Neural Networks to Neuromorphic AI
items.summary: The tension between the established technologies of connectionist AI and their neuromorphic challengers is attracting growing attention, above all because of the enormous energy demand of the former and the low power consumption of the latter. Developing and running large AI models consumes gigawatt- to terawatt-hours of energy, while the human brain operates on a continuous 20 watts. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) counter this energy demand with a frugal approach and bring elements of self-organization into the methodological repertoire of AI: local learning instead of global error backpropagation, event-driven computing, and time as a carrier of information. items.title: Neuromorphic design of a rhythmic network
items.summary: Central Pattern Generators (CPGs) have long inspired the design of rhythms that combine endogenous generation and exogenous interaction. In neurodynamics and engineering studies, CPGs have been primarily analysed and designed as networks of coupled oscillators. In contrast, the present article regards CPGs as networks that propagate events through excitable rather than oscillatory nodes. The proposed event-based perspective reduces the design of network-level rhythmic properties to the tuning of local nodal input-output characteristics. items.title: Hardware-Aware Model Inversion in Memristive Spiking Neural Networks
items.summary: Hardware-accelerated spiking neural networks (SNNs) implemented on memristive crossbar arrays offer significant gains in energy efficiency, while device variability and analog noise are sometimes assumed to hinder information extraction. However, whether these hardware effects improve, preserve, or degrade privacy after deployment remains largely unexplored. Therefore, we ask whether model-inversion leakage characterized on an SNN remains representative after the same model is mapped to a non-ideal memristive substrate, and how hardware non-idealities and reliability faults affecting synapses, neuron thresholds, and spike processing reshape that leakage. items.title: Event-SAMA: Language-Grounded Video Object Segmentation on Neuromorphic Event Streams
items.summary: Event cameras offer microsecond temporal resolution, high dynamic range and no motion blur, but referring video object segmentation (RVOS) lacks event-stream datasets and models. We introduce Event-SAMA-239K, a synthetic-event conversion of the SAMA-239K grounded video-chat corpus and all additional SAMA training data: 30,650 video clips and 392,162 images. Optical-flow, FILM or saccade upsampling followed by a linear event generator preserves all mask, referring-expression and dialogue annotations. We also introduce Event-SAMA, adapting SAMA-4B with a two-channel polarity patch embedding initialised from pretrained RGB weights and a zero-initialised event adapter. End-to-end training…

items.title: Non-Volatile Memory Devices for Neuromorphic Computing
items.summary: This chapter explores the critical role of emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) devices in advancing neuromorphic computing. Inspired by the human brain's remarkable ability to perform complex tasks like pattern recognition and adaptation, neuromorphic computing offers immense potential for implementing complex neural networks (NNs) in real hardware. Despite ongoing research into the brain's complexities, its fundamental operation relies on neurons (processing units communicating via electrochemical signals) and synapses (junctions between neurons). items.title: GC-LIF: Spiking Group-Equivariant Neural Network With Group-Coupled Membrane Dynamics
items.summary: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) promise event-driven, low-power inference, but on vision tasks they still acquire rotation invariance only through data augmentation. Group-equivariant CNNs build such symmetries into the architecture, yet a faithful spiking analogue is missing: a leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron placed after a $G$-equivariant convolution can break equivariance through its membrane recurrence. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for this not to happen. The layer is equivariant at every time step if and only if the neuron parameters $(β, v_{\mathrm{th}})$ are constant along the joint orbits of the group action on the (group, space) index. items.title: Large-$N$ limit of chiral quiver theories: free energy, supersymmetric indices and operator counting
items.summary: We find the first analytic solution to the large-$N$ saddle point equations for the $S^3$ free energy of a chiral $\mathcal N=2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory with an M-theory dual. items.title: TabCUQ: Context-Uncertainty Quantification for Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: Tabular foundation models use in-context learning to estimate conditional expected outcomes and average treatment effects for specific groups of individuals. Using these estimates to guide scientific decisions requires reliable uncertainty quantification. The challenge is to account simultaneously for two sources of uncertainty: limited-context bias and context variation arising from the small labeled sample supplied at inference. Predictive spread does not directly quantify both sources of uncertainty, and we observe that the ordinary bootstrap may substantially overestimate context variation, whereas subsampling may underestimate it. items.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability.
items.summary: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. items.title: Monocular and Multi-View Geometry-Collaborated Multi-View Stereo Network.
items.summary: Learning-based multi-view stereo methods still struggle in ill-posed regions such as repetitive patterns, textureless and occluded areas, where photometric consistency fails to provide reliable matching cues. items.title: The dynamics of large biomolecular assemblies.
items.summary: With recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy/cryo-electron tomography (cryoEM/cryoET), computational capabilities and machine learning, there has been an incredible increase in the speed of structure determination for large biomolecular assemblies. items.summary: The mechanics of liquid-liquid phase-separated (LLPS) condensates are commonly interpreted using a capillary-fluid picture, in which droplet response is governed by interfacial tension and viscous dissipation. This framework explains many synthetic coacervates and simple phase-separated liquids, but its applicability to biomolecular condensates containing transient multivalent molecular networks remains uncertain. items.title: A Biophysical Framework for Force-Induced Mitochondrial Branches.
items.summary: Mitochondrial networks are shaped not only by fission and fusion but also by mechanical forces. Here, we examine pulling-induced branch formation and contrast it with fusion-based branch formation. Live imaging reveals that branches formed by pulling are shorter-lived but initiate more frequently and with a narrower range of angles, concomitantly inducing deformation in parent mitochondria - in contrast with those formed by fusion. items.summary: To elucidate the mechanisms underlying therapy-induced resistance, we investigated the temporal dynamics of the polyploid giant cancer cell (PGCC) life cycle following treatment with the microtubule-destabilizing agent vincristine (VCR). items.summary: To investigate the impact of corneal nerve injury on meibomian glands (MG) and elucidate underlying mechanisms. Using a murine unilateral corneal trephination model, we evaluated nerve density (βIII-tubulin), MG lipogenesis, cytokine expression (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-17), inflammatory cell infiltration, and apoptosis at 2 weeks. items.title: Microtubule organisation by motors and nonmotor microtubule-associated proteins.
items.summary: Microtubules are key components of the eukaryotic cytoskeleton. These stiff polymers often span the entire cell, provide structural support, and act as tracks for long-distance transport and force generators. Their organisation underlies the logistics of intracellular cargo transport, resistance to compressive loads, and polarity factor signalling. Microtubules are intrinsically dynamic and many factors that bind to the inside, outside, and ends of the microtubule modulate their properties. items.title: Kinesin-12 (Kif15) in Neurons: From Mitotic Motor to Activity-Dependent Regulator of Dendritic Spines.
items.summary: Kinesin-12 (Kif15) is a canonical mitotic kinesin that crosslinks parallel microtubules and suppresses microtubule catastrophe. It exists in both dimeric and tetrameric oligomerization states that are regulated by ionic conditions and binding partners. Its persistent expression in postmitotic neurons indicates that this ancestral microtubule-organizing activity has been repurposed for neuronal functions, yet the dendritic role of Kif15 has remained poorly defined. items.summary: Kinetoplastid parasites, including Trypanosoma cruzi, possess a highly organized subpellicular microtubule network essential for maintaining cell shape, organelle positioning, and dividing. Here we describe results obtained using immunofluorescence microscopy of cells processed using conventional ultrastructure expansion microscopy (U-ExM), that improved visualization of the cytoskeletal structures, with an ~4.5-fold expansion, as well as the recently described and iterative ultrastructure expansion microscopy (iU-ExM) with about 6.2-fold and 18-fold expansion of epimastigotes of T. cruzi. items.title: NeuroWave-GO: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Scalable and Perception-Aware SNN-to-NoC Mapping.
items.summary: Large-scale spiking neural network (SNN)-to-network-on-chip (NoC) mapping faces two bottlenecks: topology-only graphs underrepresent temporal communication dynamics, causing a perception bottleneck, while neuron-level optimization scales poorly, causing a scalability bottleneck. items.summary: Nonvolatile memories based on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their atomic-scale thickness, low energy operation, and prolonged data storage capability. However, most reported vdW floating-gate memories employ a bottom-floating-gate configuration, which often leads to a limited on/off ratio due to charge leakage and substrate-induced disturbance. items.title: Ultra-Efficient Memristive Voltage-Resistance Logic Framework With Integrated Readout Strategy Based on Hafnium Zirconium Oxide.
items.summary: The integration of logic operations and data storage is regarded as a promising strategy for enabling edge computing, a key requirement for real-time, data-intensive scientific and industrial applications. Achieving edge-capable computing, however, requires exceptional spatiotemporal efficiency, and many previously proposed logic schemes still face substantial limitations. Here, we introduce a memristive voltage-resistance (V-R) logic strategy that infers output resistance states without additional incurring area or latency penalties. items.title: Chemically Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Electronics for Neurochemical Homeostasis
items.summary: Abstract Neuromorphic devices excel at emulating synaptic and neuronal computation, yet their states are predominantly programmed by electrical signals, limiting their ability to directly perceive and adapt to the molecular signals that govern biological neural function. Here we introduce chemical reconfiguration into neuromorphic electronics and develop a chemically reconfigurable neuromorphic healer (CR-NeuroHealer), in which molecular inputs directly reprogram synaptic plasticity to couple neurochemical perception with adaptive regulation. items.title: Dual-Mode Memristors with Controlled Cluster Dynamics for High-Performance Neuromorphic Computing.
items.summary: In the process of realizing brain-like information processing based on artificial synapses, the conductive filament (CF) model has become an intensively studied topic. items.title: Electro-optical memristors: from the origin to device implementation.
items.summary: With the rapid growth of artificial intelligence, conventional von Neumann architectures face increasing limitations arising from memory-processor separation, high data-transfer latency, and power consumption. Memristive devices offer a promising route towards in-memory and neuromorphic computing by combining information storage and processing within compact two-terminal structures. items.title: A three-terminal MoTe 2 artificial synapse with electrical and optical dual-mode plasticity.
items.summary: Artificial synaptic devices capable of integrating sensing, memory, and computing functions are highly desirable for next-generation neuromorphic systems. However, most reported artificial synapses rely on single-mode electrical or optical stimulation, limiting their ability to achieve multimodal perception and adaptive information processing. Here, we demonstrate a three-terminal artificial synaptic device based on MoTe 2 flakes that enables both electrical and optical synaptic modulation within a unified device architecture. items.summary: This essay challenges the prevailing assumption that the goal of artificial intelligence should be increasingly general intelligence. It proposes an alternative model: “AI prodigies” — systems engineered for superhuman capability within deliberately bounded domains while remaining intentionally incomplete outside them. items.summary: As AI becomes increasingly integrated into daily life and high-stakes decision-making, aligning it with human moral judgments is a challenge of profound importance.
